note: Changes to the model or the data process, each tied to the graded result or data problem that prompted it. Newest first.

lessons.saw: Ten research agents shared one search budget of about 200 searches and ran out partway through, so several props have no per-90 rates and some XIs have only one source. Typed KickOff URLs were also refused; only links that came back from a search could be opened.
lessons.change: Each match agent searches for its KickOff and statz.ai pages first, opens the links the search returns, and keeps to about 15 searches so every match gets covered.

lessons.saw: Japan v Brazil kicked off at 11:15 Warsaw. By then the morning run had found no bookmaker prices and no team sheets for it.
lessons.change: Games that kick off before noon Warsaw are researched first, in their own quick pass. If they still have no prices, they are left off the page.

lessons.saw: The data check priced picks without the track-record adjustment the site applies, so it could report a different best bet from the page.
lessons.change: The check now loads results.json first, so it prints the same best bets the page shows.

lessons.saw: KickOff lists bet365 prices as fractions (11/20, 10/3), and two research passes could not open the page at all.
lessons.change: Fractions are converted to decimals (11/20 becomes 1.55). If KickOff can’t be read, the run tries it again before using another site, and the odds note names the bookmaker and the site.

lessons.saw: Argentina v Uruguay kicks off at 23:00 UK time, which is midnight in Warsaw.
lessons.change: Matches are filed by their Warsaw date, so a midnight kick-off goes on the next day’s page.

lessons.saw: One source listed Florian Wirtz at 2.15 fouls per 90, which looked like fouls won rather than fouls committed.
lessons.change: Foul props only use fouls committed. A figure above about 1.5 per 90 for an attacking player is checked against a second source before it is used.

lessons.saw: Some sources count a player’s shots over more games than the team totals beside them, which inflates his share of the team’s chances.
lessons.change: Team totals must cover the same games as the player counts, or they are left out.

lessons.saw: 4 of 5 props lost, including 1+ shot on target for Anthony Gordon (1.30) and Fermín López (1.29). Those prices need the bet to land 77% of the time.
lessons.change: Each prop now gets its own chance from the player’s per-90 rates, or a cautious position average, and is only marked Bet when that chance beats the price.

lessons.saw: France to win + Over 1.5 goals lost when Italy won 3-1. France were only a 46% favourite. Builders on 55%+ favourites won 2 of 3.
lessons.change: A builder only includes a result leg when the favourite is 55% or more. Otherwise it is built from double chance, goals and BTTS legs.

lessons.saw: Two -1.5 handicaps had no bookmaker price. Spain’s won 2-0; England’s lost on a 2-1 win.
lessons.change: Handicaps without a bookmaker price stop at -1, which refunds the stake on a one-goal win.

lessons.saw: Over 7.5 corners in Italy v France and England to win the corner count both lost. Neither had a bookmaker line to anchor it.
lessons.change: Corner and card chances priced without a bookmaker line are pulled 20% closer to 50/50.

lessons.saw: The best-bet tile could show a pick whose price was shorter than the model’s fair odds, so backing it had no edge.
lessons.change: The best bet must be priced between 1.35 and 3.50 and within 2% of fair value or better. When nothing qualifies, the card says No bet.

lessons.saw: Picks were shown but never graded, so nothing told the model which markets it overrated.
lessons.change: Every graded pick goes into the track record. Once a market has 8 results, its chances are pulled toward 50/50 if it lands less often than promised, or stretched if it lands more often.
